lessons.title: Profiles are the customer, not the contact
lessons.why: The contact ends. The profile is how the next contact knows who called.
paras: Customer Profiles stores the customer and the objects you attach. Connect-only profiles are priced at 0 USD per daily use in the appendix. The moment you merge imported CRM data, daily use of that profile is 0.005 USD, with extra charges past each 100 objects, and a cap described in the appendix.
The flow block can get, create, and update a profile. Identity resolution decides when two records are one person. Get that rule wrong and agents see two half-customers.
points: Keys on an object type default to 10.
A profile object maxes at 250 KB in the quota table. All objects on one profile share a larger cap.
Calculated attributes and event triggers have their own quotas.
E911 addresses for agents are stored here on purpose. That is a different profile population from customers. Do not mix the matching rules carelessly.
lessons.mistake: Using the phone number as the only key when customers share a household line.

number.n: Per profile, per day it is used

lessons.title: Cases survive the transfer
lessons.why: A case is the issue. Contacts are the attempts to close it.
paras: Cases entered preview on 20 June 2022 and became generally available on 3 October 2022. You get fields, templates, layouts, related items, and SLAs. Defaults include 5 domains per account and 10 SLAs on a case.
The Cases block gets, updates, and creates. Create the case before you transfer if the next agent should see it. The case id should be a contact attribute.
points: Related items default to 200. Files on a case default to 50.
A template with 50 custom fields is the ceiling and it is not adjustable.
Status values are a contract with the CRM if both systems have a case. Pick one system of record.
Closing a contact does not close a case unless you said so.
lessons.mistake: Opening a new case for every menu retry in the IVR.

lessons.title: Tasks are the channel with no audio
lessons.why: A promise to call back, a form to review, and a follow-up are tasks. They have quotas and an expiry.
paras: Create task starts a task contact and a flow. Agents work tasks from a routing profile that includes the task channel. The default concurrent quota is 2500 active tasks, including ACW. You can schedule a task up to 90 days out and reschedule it at most 20 times.

Basic task price in the appendix's Basic table is 0.04 USD per task created. Connect Customer lists 0.070 USD per task in the engagement table. Read the row that matches the product form you bought. This campus labels both as list prices, not a quote.
points: Task templates: 50 per instance, not adjustable, with 50 custom fields.
A task flow can still call Lambda.
Do not use a voice queue for work that has no call.
Expiry and assignment are visible in metrics. Alarm on age.
lessons.mistake: Sending follow-up work to a shared mailbox and also creating a task.

lessons.title: One customer, three objects
lessons.why: Profile, case, and contact answer different questions. Collapsing them makes reporting lie.
paras: The profile answers who. The case answers which issue. The contact answers what happened at 10:41. Store the profile id and the case id as attributes so the CTR, the workspace, and the CRM activity all name them.
Customer Profiles can integrate with Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk, and others. That feed is how the profile stays current. It is not a reason to stop writing the ids onto the contact.
points: Search before create, or you duplicate people.
A task can attach to the same case.
Deletes and merges are identity-resolution events. Tell the CRM.
Retention of profile objects is a privacy decision. The quota allows a long expiry. Your policy may not.
lessons.mistake: Using the ContactId as the customer id.
